stories.headline: Zhipu's GLM-5.2 tops Artificial Analysis as leading open-weights model with score of 51

key_facts.fact: GLM-5.2 scores 51 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1, the highest among open-weights models and ahead of MiniMax-M3 (44), DeepSeek V4 Pro max (44) and Kimi K2.6 (43).
key_facts.excerpt: GLM-5.2 is the leading open weights model on the Intelligence Index v4.1. At 51, it leads MiniMax-M3 (44), DeepSeek V4 Pro (max, 44) and Kimi K2.6 (43).

key_facts.fact: Among frontier models overall, GLM-5.2 (51) trails only Fable 5 (60), Opus 4.8 (56) and GPT-5.5 (55) on the index — placing it on the Pareto frontier of intelligence vs cost per task.
key_facts.excerpt: Z ai's GLM-5.2 is the new leading open weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index scoring 51 and it sits on the Pareto frontier of Intelligence vs Cost per Task

key_facts.fact: The model retains the GLM-5.1 architecture footprint at 744B total parameters with 40B active per inference, but expands the context window from 200K to 1M tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: The architecture behind the score is 744B total parameters with 40B active parameters per inference call, the same footprint as its predecessor GLM-5.1, but the context window has expanded from 200K to 1M tokens.

key_facts.fact: Capability gains concentrate in scientific reasoning: CritPt +16 points to 21%, Humanity's Last Exam +12 points to 40%, SciCode +7 points to 50%; GDPval-AA v2 reaches 1524 versus 1514 for proprietary GPT-5.5.
key_facts.excerpt: CritPt improved 16 points to 21%, Humanity's Last Exam climbed 12 points to 40%, and SciCode rose 7 points to 50%. On the GDPval-AA v2 metric, GLM-5.2 reached 1524, landing in comparable territory to proprietary GPT-5.5 at 1514

key_facts.fact: On FrontierSWE, a long-horizon coding benchmark, GLM-5.2 trails Opus 4.8 by 1% while edging past GPT-5.5 by 1% and Opus 4.7 by 11%.
key_facts.excerpt: On this benchmark, GLM-5.2 trails Opus 4.8 by only 1%, while edging out GPT-5.5 by 1% and Opus 4.7 by 11%.

key_facts.fact: GLM-5.2 is priced at $1.4/$4.4/$0.26 per 1M input/output/cache-hit tokens on Zhipu's first-party API and is released under an MIT license with weights on HuggingFace and ModelScope.
key_facts.excerpt: On the first-party API it is priced in line with GLM-5.1 at $1.4/$4.4/$0.26 per 1M input/output/cache hit tokens

stories.headline: About 200 Glasswing firms keep Mythos Preview access despite US shutdown order

key_facts.fact: Roughly 200 organizations enrolled in Anthropic's Project Glasswing program have preserved access to Mythos Preview after a US government order forced the broader public Mythos rollout to be shut down.
key_facts.excerpt: The Claude maker had limited Mythos Preview to about 200 organizations, including the U.S. government, under its Glasswing program after the model identified thousands of software vulnerabilities.

key_facts.fact: Cybersecurity firms Dragos and Cisco Systems confirmed to Bloomberg they have retained access to Mythos Preview through Glasswing.
key_facts.excerpt: Firms such as Dragos and Cisco Systems confirmed to Bloomberg News that they had retained access to Mythos Preview.

key_facts.fact: European cybersecurity agency ENISA, invited to join Glasswing before the US block, was told its planned access would be revoked.
key_facts.excerpt: European cybersecurity agency Enisa, which had been invited to join Glasswing ahead of the U.S. government's block, was informed on Friday it would no longer be given access

key_facts.fact: Glasswing partners use Mythos Preview to scan codebases for vulnerabilities; the model has surfaced more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity flaws across participating organizations.
key_facts.excerpt: they've been deploying the model to scan their codebases for vulnerabilities. We recently described how these partners have so far found more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity security flaws.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is committing up to $100M in Mythos Preview usage credits to Glasswing participants, with model pricing of $25/$125 per 1M input/output tokens for paid use after the preview.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's commitment of $100M in model usage credits to Project Glasswing and additional participants will cover substantial usage throughout this research preview. Afterward, Claude Mythos Preview will be available to participants at $25/$125 per million input/output tokens

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's relationship with the US government ruptured this year after it refused to allow military use of its models for domestic surveillance or fully autonomous weapons systems.
key_facts.excerpt: IPO-bound Anthropic's relationship with the government ruptured this year after it refused to allow the U.S. military to use its AI models for domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons systems.

stories.headline: Google guarantees $3.2B for New York data center supplying TPUs to Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Google provided a $3.2 billion financial guarantee for a New York data center that will host Anthropic's workloads on Google's own TPUs (tensor processing units).
key_facts.excerpt: Google provided a $3.2 billion financial guarantee for the project to boost its AI chip game and challenge NVIDIA's lead. The company is backing Anthropic by powering its work with Google's own TPUs (tensor processing units) at a huge New York data center

key_facts.fact: The move mirrors Nvidia's strategy of seeding demand for its own silicon by funding data centers that run on those chips; Google is also expanding direct TPU sales to external customers.
key_facts.excerpt: pretty much mirroring how NVIDIA encourages demand for its GPUs … Google isn't stopping there: it's now planning to sell TPUs directly to more customers and has rolled out a new chip designed for faster, cheaper AI processing.

key_facts.fact: Google has agreed to backstop lease payments at five US data centers (in New York, Texas, Louisiana, and Indiana), enabling a $35 billion chip financing package that locks Anthropic onto Google's TPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: Google has agreed to backstop lease payments at five U.S. data centers, enabling a $35 billion chip financing deal that locks Anthropic into Google's custom TPU ecosystem for years to come

key_facts.fact: Broadcom provides a residual-value guarantee on the $31 billion senior tranche, aligning the senior debt with Broadcom's investment-grade credit rather than Anthropic's.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom provides an additional residual‑value guarantee on the $31 billion senior tranche, meaning if Anthropic defaults and the used TPUs can't be resold for enough to cover the loan, Broadcom absorbs the shortfall.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic continues to run a multi-cloud, multi-accelerator stack — AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and Nvidia GPUs — with Amazon as its primary cloud and training partner.
key_facts.excerpt: We train and run Claude on a range of AI hardware—AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and NVIDIA GPUs … Amazon remains our primary cloud provider and training partner

stories.headline: General Intuition in talks to raise $300M at ~$2B from Bezos, Schmidt for spatial-AI agents

key_facts.fact: New York-based General Intuition is in talks to raise around $300 million at a valuation of just over $2 billion to train AI agents in spatial-temporal reasoning.
key_facts.excerpt: General Intuition, the New York-based startup building a foundation model that trains AI agents how to move through space and time, is in talks to raise around $300 million … The fresh funds would bring the startup's valuation up to just over $2 billion

key_facts.fact: Backers in the new round include Jeff Bezos and Eric Schmidt, plus existing investors Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst.
key_facts.excerpt: General Intuition has secured funds from backers, including Jeff Bezos and Eric Schmidt, as well as existing investors Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst.

key_facts.fact: The round comes only eight months after the company's $134M seed and quadruples its valuation; total funding will exceed $400M in under a year.
key_facts.excerpt: General Intuition launched eight months ago with a $134 million seed round. The new valuation is about four times that … the financing would bring the startup's total funding to more than $400 million in less than a year.

key_facts.fact: The startup trains embodied AI and world models on roughly 2 billion video game clips per year from Medal's 10 million monthly active users — first-person, interactive footage rather than spectator-perspective gameplay.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup trains embodied AI and world models using Medal's dataset of 2 billion videos per year from 10 million monthly active users … unique because it allows AI to learn from interactive, first-person gameplay

key_facts.fact: General Intuition rejected a reported ~$500M acquisition offer from OpenAI before pursuing the raise.
key_facts.excerpt: General Intuition, the AI lab that spun out of gaming clip platform Medal after rejecting a reported $500 million offer from OpenAI, is raising approximately $300 million at a valuation of just over $2 billion.

key_facts.fact: The capital will scale compute capacity to ship a new product by late summer or early fall.
key_facts.excerpt: General Intuition will use the funds to scale up its compute capacity so it can release a new product by the end of summer or early fall

stories.headline: Meta contracts ~1.6 GW of AI compute from Crusoe across Texas and Missouri sites

key_facts.fact: Meta Platforms has signed new agreements with Crusoe to obtain roughly 1.6 gigawatts of combined AI computing capacity at Crusoe data centers in Childress, Texas and Warrenton, Missouri.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta will purchase computing capacity from Crusoe's data centres located in Childress, Texas, and Warrenton, Missouri … approximately 1.6 gigawatts (GW) of combined capacity across the two sites

key_facts.fact: Financial terms and delivery timelines for the deal were not disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: Details regarding the financial value of the agreements … the specific timeline for delivery of the … capacity were not disclosed.

key_facts.fact: Crusoe currently holds 4.9 GW of contracted capacity across an overall pipeline exceeding 40 GW, with existing customers including Oracle, OpenAI, Microsoft and Google.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier this month, Crusoe announced it held contracts for a total of 4.9GW in capacity, with over 40GW in its overall project pipeline … The 4.9GW figure encompasses ongoing projects for Oracle, OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google

key_facts.fact: Last month Crusoe, Blue Owl Capital and Primary Digital Infrastructure began the second phase of a $15B joint venture to build a 1.2 GW AI data center in Abilene, Texas.
key_facts.excerpt: Crusoe, Blue Owl Capital, and Primary Digital Infrastructure began the second phase of their $15bn joint venture to build a 1.2GW AI data centre in Abilene, Texas.

key_facts.fact: Crusoe's broader buildout now exceeds 3.4 GW of planned and operational capacity, including a 1.8 GW project underway in Wyoming.
key_facts.excerpt: A separate 1.8-gigawatt project in Wyoming is already underway, contributing to a growing network that now exceeds 3.4 gigawatts of planned and operational capacity

stories.headline: Amazon in talks to sell Trainium AI chips for use in third-party data centers

key_facts.fact: Amazon's senior vice president overseeing semiconductor, AI and quantum, Peter DeSantis, said AWS is in talks to sell its Trainium AI chips for use in other companies' data centers — chips previously exclusive to AWS.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon's AI chief Peter DeSantis told Bloomberg that AWS is in talks to sell its AI chip Trainium to other companies for use in data centers.

key_facts.fact: DeSantis said a key driver is rising international demand — particularly in Europe — for locally controlled, sovereign AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: a major driver behind the push is rising international demand for locally controlled computing resources — particularly in Europe, where regulatory and political pressure has increased calls for sovereign AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: DeSantis dismissed concerns the external sales would cannibalize AWS cloud revenue, citing 'so much underconsumption in AI.'
key_facts.excerpt: "There's so much underconsumption in AI. I'm not worried about it," he said.

key_facts.fact: CEO Andy Jassy estimated in April that selling Amazon's chips at run-rate to AWS and outside customers could push the chip business toward ~$50B in annualized revenue, up from a current ~$20B run rate across Trainium, Graviton and Nitro.
key_facts.excerpt: putting the company's annualized chip revenue at roughly $20 billion across the Trainium, Graviton, and Nitro product lines. Jassy wrote at the time that selling to both AWS and external customers could push that figure toward $50 billion annually.

key_facts.fact: Trainium-line revenue commitments exceed $225 billion as of April, and Trainium4 is already booked more than a year ahead of shipment.
key_facts.excerpt: Trainium sold out almost right away, and Trainium4 is already booked more than a year before launch.

key_facts.fact: The move mirrors a similar shift by Google, which has begun selling its custom TPUs to select external data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: The approach follows a similar path taken by Google, which recently announced plans to sell its custom chips to select external data centers.

stories.headline: Ex-White House AI adviser Dean Ball joins OpenAI to lead new Strategic Futures team

key_facts.fact: Dean Ball, former Senior Policy Adviser for AI and Emerging Technology in the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, will join OpenAI on July 6 as head of a new team called Strategic Futures.
key_facts.excerpt: our colleague Dean W. Ball is joining OpenAI as Head of Strategic Futures on July 6.

key_facts.fact: Strategic Futures will report to Chief Strategy Officer Jason Kwon and span both public-facing policy proposals and OpenAI's internal governance, working with the Preparedness, legal, policy, National Security and Global Affairs teams.
key_facts.excerpt: its work will cover both public-facing policy (for example, proposals for legislation) and internal governance within the lab, working in close collaboration with members of the technical staff, the Preparedness team, the legal team, policy staff from the National Security and Global Affairs teams

key_facts.fact: The team's mandate explicitly covers catastrophic risk, recursive self-improvement, labor market impact and the relationship between frontier labs and government.
key_facts.excerpt: charged with shaping frontier AI policy, which is to say matters pertaining to: catastrophic risk, recursive self-improvement, labor market impact, and the relationship between the frontier labs, governments (particularly the U.S. Federal Government), and society.

key_facts.fact: Ball co-authored the White House AI Action Plan released last summer and previously was a senior fellow at the Foundation for American Innovation — a role he will retain on a non-resident basis.
key_facts.excerpt: Few people have shaped AI policy as directly as Dean, from his writing at Hyperdimensional, to his co-authorship of the White House AI Action Plan … Happily, Dean will stay on with FAI as a non-resident senior fellow

key_facts.fact: Ball has publicly criticized the Trump administration's actions against Anthropic, including the Pentagon's designation of the company as a supply-chain risk and the White House's export limits on Anthropic's Fable model.
key_facts.excerpt: Ball has also previously criticized the Trump administration's dispute with Anthropic, including the Pentagon's designation of the company as a … chain risk and the White House's export limits on Anthropic's Fable AI model

key_facts.fact: The hire follows OpenAI's recent recruitment of Noam Shazeer from Google to lead architecture research.
key_facts.excerpt: His appointment follows closely on the heels of the company successfully recruiting AI expert Noam Shazeer from Google.
